comment: The methodology presents a Client Registry as recurrent and required. A client registry may be valuable for longitudinal care, but it is not universally required for a DPI-H entry point. Aggregate HMIS, event-based surveillance or services that must operate for unknown or undocumented persons. Labeling it required may drive premature identity-centric architecture and unnecessary linkage risk.

reviewer.name: Brian O'Donnell (on behalf of HISP-UiO)
reviewer.organisation: HISP Centre at University of Oslo

public.text: The methodology presents a Client Registry as recurrent and required. A client registry may be valuable for longitudinal care, but it is not universally required for a DPI-H entry point. Aggregate HMIS, event-based surveillance or services that must operate for unknown or undocumented persons. Labeling it required may drive premature identity-centric architecture and unnecessary linkage risk.
public.suggestedRevision: Change ‘required’ to ‘frequently useful where the priority use cases require person matching’. Require a necessity and proportionality test, identity-optional workflows, temporary/pseudonymous identifiers and a documented alternative for contexts without universal or trusted identification.
